concepts.def: Blended family — formed after divorce/remarriage; increasingly common in France since the 1980s.
Pacte civil de solidarité — civil union introduced in 1999, open to same-sex and opposite-sex couples.
Parenthood — covers shared roles of mothers and fathers; congé parental is parental leave.
Same-sex marriage legalised in France in 2013 under the Taubira law.
Verbs like se marier, s'entendre, se disputer that take être in the passé composé and agree with the subject.
Divorce — roughly 45% of French marriages end in divorce; consensual divorce was simplified in 2017.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit 1: Speaking — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit 1: Speaking brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit 1: Speaking.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
